subject: Polity
topic: Historical Background of the Constitution – Final 110% Set

mcqs.q: Consider the following pairs: (Act – Key Provision) 1. Regulating Act, 1773 – Court of Directors 2. Pitt’s India Act, 1784 – Board of Control 3. Charter Act, 1813 – Lapse of Company’s trade monopoly except tea and China. Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
Under the Regulating Act, 1773, the Governor of Bengal was elevated to Governor-General of Bengal. Who among the following was the first such Governor-General?
Which of the following correctly describes the change introduced by Pitt’s India Act, 1784?

options.A: It abolished the Board of Control and created the Court of Directors.
options.B: It distinguished between commercial and political functions of the Company.
options.C: It transferred all powers of the Company to the British Crown.
options.D: It introduced separate electorates for the first time.

mcqs.q: The Charter Act of 1813 is known for which of the following? 1. Ending the Company’s trade monopoly except tea and trade with China. 2. Granting one lakh rupees for education. 3. Allowing Christian missionaries to propagate religion. Select the correct answer:
Which of the following was a consequence of the Charter Act, 1833?

options.A: A law member was added to the Governor-General’s Council.
options.B: The Governor-General of Bengal became Governor-General of India.
options.C: Commercial activities of the Company were completely ended.

mcqs.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Charter Act of 1853: 1. It separated legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General’s council. 2. It introduced an open competition system for the Indian Civil Services. 3. It extended the Company’s rule for another 20 years. Which of the statements is/are correct?
Which of the following Acts abolished the system of double government introduced by Pitt’s India Act?

The Government of India Act, 1858 transferred power from the Company to the Crown. Which of the following was created by this Act? 1. Secretary of State for India. 2. Council of India. 3. Viceroy of India. Select the correct answer:
Who was the first Viceroy of India under the Government of India Act, 1858?

Consider the following features: 1. Decentralization of legislative powers 2. Portfolio system 3. Ordinance-making power of the Governor-General. Which of the above were introduced by the Indian Councils Act, 1861?
Under the Indian Councils Act, 1861, the Governor-General’s ordinance remained in force for:

options.D: Until the next session of the British Parliament

mcqs.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Indian Councils Act, 1892?

options.A: It introduced direct elections for the first time.
options.B: It granted legislative councils the power to ask questions on matters of public interest.
options.C: It provided separate electorates for Muslims.
options.D: It introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

mcqs.q: The term 'portfolio system' refers to:

options.A: Division of work among members of the Viceroy's council.
options.B: Establishment of legislative councils in provinces.
options.C: Separation of central and provincial budgets.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Acts introduced separate communal electorates for Muslims?

Consider the following provisions: 1. Separate electorates for Muslims. 2. Appointment of an Indian to the Viceroy's executive council. 3. Introduction of dyarchy in provinces. Which of these were part of the Indian Councils Act, 1909?
The Montagu Declaration of 1917 promised:

options.B: Gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to responsible government.

mcqs.q: Which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? 1. Government of India Act, 1919 – Introduction of dyarchy in provinces. 2. Government of India Act, 1919 – Bicameral legislature at the Centre. 3. Government of India Act, 1919 – Separation of provincial budgets from the central budget. Select the correct answer:
Dyarchy in the provinces, under the Act of 1919, meant:

options.A: Division of subjects between the Centre and the provinces.
options.B: Division of provincial subjects into 'transferred' and 'reserved' categories.
options.C: Dual government of British and Indian ministers at the Centre.
options.D: Joint rule by the Governor-General and the Secretary of State.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was NOT a feature of the Government of India Act, 1919?

The Nehru Report (1928) recommended all the following EXCEPT:

options.C: Federal structure with residuary powers to the Centre.

mcqs.q: The Communal Award of 1932 provided for:

options.B: Separate electorates for the Depressed Classes.
options.C: Reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in joint electorates.

mcqs.q: The Poona Pact (1932) between Gandhi and Ambedkar modified the Communal Award by:

options.A: Abolishing separate electorates for Depressed Classes and providing reserved seats.
options.C: Granting separate electorates to all backward classes.
options.D: Rejecting the concept of joint electorates entirely.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Round Table Conferences was attended by Mahatma Gandhi as the sole representative of the Congress?
The Government of India Act, 1935, was based on the recommendations of:

options.B: Simon Commission Report and Round Table Conferences

mcqs.q: Consider the following features: 1. Establishment of an All-India Federation. 2. Division of legislative powers into three lists. 3. Dyarchy at the Centre. Which of the above were part of the Government of India Act, 1935?
Why did the All-India Federation under the Government of India Act, 1935, never come into existence?

options.A: The British government refused to implement it.
options.B: The requisite number of princely states did not accede.
options.C: The Indian National Congress rejected the plan.
options.D: World War II broke out immediately.

options.A: It had original jurisdiction in fundamental rights cases.
options.B: It was the highest court of appeal from the High Courts.
options.C: It could issue writs for enforcement of fundamental rights.
options.D: It was directly under the Privy Council.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Acts provided for the establishment of the Reserve Bank of India?
The August Offer (1940) promised:

options.B: Expansion of the Viceroy's Executive Council with more Indians and a Constituent Assembly after the war.

options.B: Formation of an interim government with equal Hindu and Muslim representation.

mcqs.q: Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946): 1. It rejected the demand for a separate Pakistan. 2. It proposed a federal structure with a weak centre. 3. It recommended grouping of provinces into three sections. Which of the above is/are correct?
Under the Cabinet Mission Plan, the Union would have subjects like:

options.B: All subjects except those given to provinces.
options.D: No subjects; all powers were with the provinces.

mcqs.q: Which of the following groups under the Cabinet Mission Plan was strongly opposed by the Congress?
The Mountbatten Plan (June 3 Plan) primarily provided for:

options.B: Partition of India and transfer of power to two Dominions.
options.C: A united India with a weak centre.
options.D: Continuation of British rule for ten years.

options.B: Appointed by the British Crown and acted as a constitutional head.

Which of the above is/are correct?
